extracted.intended_audience: national football associations, team delegations, match officials and organisers involved in the FIFA World Cup 2022 preliminary competition
extracted.subtask_description: Official regulations governing rights, duties, organisation, match operations and COVID-19 requirements for the FIFA World Cup 2022 preliminary competition. Covers entry, player eligibility, match conduct, disciplinary, medical and media obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binding nature of the Regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Regulations for the FIFA World Cup 2022™ Preliminary Competition ... regulate the rights, duties and responsibilities of all associations taking part ... The Regulations and all directives, decisions, guidelines and circulars issued by FIFA shall be binding for all parties participating and involved in the preparation, organisation and hosting of FIFA World Cup 2022™ preliminary competition matches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All participants must comply with these Regulations and any FIFA directives, decisions or circulars; rights not granted remain with FIFA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organising Committee decisions final
rubrics_metrics.description: The decisions taken by the FIFA Organising Committee and/or its bureau/sub-committee are final and binding and not subject to appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Organising Committee may appoint sub-committees/bureaux for emergencies; their decisions take immediate effect and require later plenary confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct of Team Delegation Members
rubrics_metrics.description: Each participating member association shall be responsible throughout the preliminary competition for the conduct of all accreditation-bearing players, coaches, managers, officials, media officers, representatives and guests of its delegation (Team Delegation Members), and of any person carrying out duties on its behalf throughout the preliminary competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associations must ensure delegation members comply with FIFA Statutes, regulations and decisions; failure can lead to disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insurance obligations for associations and delegation members
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensuring the provision of adequate insurance to cover its Team Delegation Members and any other persons carrying out duties on its behalf against all risks, including but not limited to injury, accident, disease and travel ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host association must obtain adequate insurance for match organisation risks and identify FIFA as a named insured where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of incidental and extended-stay costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Paying for incidental expenses and for any costs incurred by its Team Delegation Members; paying for any costs of extending the stay of any member of its delegation, the duration of which is determined by FIFA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associations bear costs for their delegations and for extensions required by FIFA decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visa and travel documentation responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying for any required visas in good time from the consulate or embassy of the host country; if necessary, the assistance of the host association is to be sought as early as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associations must proactively secure visas; host association should assist when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media and press obligations of associations
rubrics_metrics.description: Attending media conferences and other official media activities organised by FIFA and/or by the host association in accordance with the applicable FIFA regulations and instructions issued by FIFA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associations must make coaches/players available for pre- and post-match media activities and appoint a media officer (see media provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with FIFA regulations and IMP / COVID-19 measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensuring that every member of its delegation complies with the FIFA Statutes, the applicable FIFA regulations ... and implementing (where applicable) the measures mandated in the FIFA International Match Protocol (IMP) and bearing the resulting costs ... All Team Delegation Members shall also fully comply with these Regulations (including the COVID-19 Regulations), the IMP and any other COVID-19-related requirements or instructions issued by FIFA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associations are responsible for enforcing IMP testing, hygiene and other COVID-19 protocols for their delegations and third parties acting on their behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indemnity to FIFA
rubrics_metrics.description: All participating member associations shall indemnify, defend and hold FIFA, and all of its officers, directors, employees, representatives, agents, and all other auxiliary persons free and harmless against any and all liabilities ... resulting from, arising out of, or attributable to, any non-compliance with these Regulations by the participating member associations, their Team Delegation Members, their affiliates and any third parties contracted to the participating member associations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associations must accept full legal and financial responsibility for breaches by their delegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host association match-hosting responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Each participating member association hosting a match ... shall be responsible, amongst other matters, for guaranteeing, planning and implementing law and order as well as safety and security in the stadiums and other relevant locations in conjunction with the relevant authorities; obtaining adequate insurance cover; providing a national stadium ... sending three copies of a DVD recording of each home match by courier to the FIFA general secretariat within 24 hours of the end of the match.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host must follow FIFA Stadium Safety and Security Regulations, secure insurance naming FIFA, make stadium available for scheduled dates, and supply match recordings promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match organisation COVID-19-specific hosting tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensuring that all measures taken in relation to team travel, transport, accommodation, logistics, match preparation and the match itself are in line with the requirements set by the relevant local authority(ies) and government; completing the football-specific risk assessment tool as mandated by the IMP; informing the visiting team ... of any exceptional requirements and restrictions in effect at the match venue due to the COVID-19 pandemic at least 14 days prior to the match date ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host must complete IMP risk assessments and communicate COVID-19 restrictions early (14 days) and update as necessary using the IMP template.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry and acceptance obligations on entering competition
rubrics_metrics.description: On entering the preliminary competition, the participating member associations and their Team Delegation Members automatically undertake to: observe and comply with the FIFA Statutes, regulations, directives, circulars, guidelines and decisions as well as national and international laws; accept that administrative, disciplinary and refereeing matters shall be dealt with by FIFA; participate with the best possible team available in all matches ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry is online via FIFA extranet and acceptance of FIFA authority and obligations (including media rights assignment) is mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: FIFA media and image rights assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Accept and fully comply with FIFA’s right to use and/or FIFA’s right to sub‑license the right to use on a non‑exclusive basis, in perpetuity and free of any charge, any of their records, names, photographs and images ... participating member associations and their Team Delegation Members shall ensure that such third party waives, pledges and unconditionally assigns and/or transfers to FIFA ... any such rights to ensure FIFA’s unfettered use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associations must guarantee that any third-party rights are assigned or waived so FIFA can use media without restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal, fines and sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any association that withdraws between the submission of the entry form and the start of the preliminary competition will be sanctioned with a fine of at least CHF 20,000. Any association that withdraws after the start of the preliminary competition will be sanctioned with a fine of at least CHF 40,000. Depending on the circumstances, further sanctions including expulsion may be imposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawals are penalised; disciplinary committee may impose additional sanctions tailored to circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unplayed/abandoned matches and sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any match which is not played or which is abandoned – except in cases of force majeure recognised by FIFA – may lead to the imposition of sanctions against the relevant associations by the FIFA Disciplinary Committee ... In such cases, the FIFA Disciplinary Committee may also order that the match be replayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FIFA assesses whether force majeure applies; if not, sanctions and replay orders possible; associations may be ordered to reimburse expenses and pay compensation.

rubrics_metrics.name: COVID-19 and force majeure (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: The COVID-19 pandemic and related circumstances are not, in and of themselves, considered cases of force majeure. However, examples ... that may be submitted to FIFA for consideration as cases of force majeure include: a) national authorities announce restrictions just before a match; b) visiting team not permitted to leave due to closed borders; c) visiting team is refused entry; d) insufficient number of match officials available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FIFA retains sole discretion to determine force majeure; COVID-19 situations may be considered case-by-case based on these examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommencement rules for abandoned matches
rubrics_metrics.description: If a match is abandoned ... the match shall recommence at the minute at which play was interrupted, and with the same scoreline; the recommencement of play must be scheduled so as to comply with the COVID-19 testing requirements as mandated in the IMP ... in general, the match shall recommence with the same players on the pitch and substitutes available as when the match was abandoned. However, if a player who was on the pitch when the match was abandoned cannot participate ... based on the result of his COVID-19 test, he may be replaced with a substitute player from the start list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommencement preserves scoreline, time and personnel except where IMP COVID-19 test results prevent participation; substitutions lists generally unchanged but COVID test outcomes may permit specific replacements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match replay scheduling and expenses after abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: The kick-off time, date (which shall always first be foreseen for the following day) and location shall be decided by FIFA in consultation with both the host and visiting associations ... For the preliminary competition, if a match still cannot be played on the third day after the match was abandoned, the expenses incurred by the visiting association shall be split between the two associations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FIFA decides replay logistics in consultation; if replay cannot occur within three days visiting association expenses are shared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility of players
rubrics_metrics.description: Each association shall ensure ... a) all players shall hold the nationality of its country and be subject to its jurisdiction; b) all players shall be eligible for selection in accordance with the FIFA Statutes, the Regulations Governing the Application of the FIFA Statutes and other relevant FIFA rules and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associations are responsible for fielding only eligible players; failure leads to consequences under the FIFA Disciplinary Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: COVID-19 testing as eligibility condition
rubrics_metrics.description: Only players who comply with and pass the testing requirements and timelines stipulated in the IMP (negative test result) are considered eligible players.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A negative test per IMP is mandatory for match eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laws of the Game and match duration
rubrics_metrics.description: All matches shall be played in accordance with the Laws of the Game in force ... Each match shall last 90 minutes, comprising two periods of 45 minutes, with a half-time interval of 15 minutes. Extra time, if applicable, consists of two periods of 15 minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: English text authoritative for interpretation discrepancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitutions (temporary Law 3 amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: During the match, each team may use a maximum of five substitutes; has a maximum of three substitution opportunities; may additionally make substitutions at half-time. Where extra time is played, each team may use an additional substitute ... and has one additional substitution opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return substitutes not allowed for senior competitions; simultaneous substitutions by both teams each count as a used substitution opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of football technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: FIFA and/or the confederation when applicable may use football technologies such as goal-line technology (GLT), a video assistant referee (VAR) system or electronic performance and tracking systems (EPTS) ... A video assistant referee (VAR) may assist the referee ... in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Laws of the Game.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technology use is subject to Laws of the Game and IFAB provisions; only qualified FIFA video match officials for VAR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refereeing appointments and qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: On-field match official appointments ... shall be proposed by the confederations to the FIFA Referees Committee for ratification. For each match, the referee and the assistant referees shall be selected from the FIFA Refereeing International List in force. Only qualified FIFA video match officials shall be selected where VAR is implemented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions of the Referees Committee are final; minimum of three match officials required; appointed officials receive official match kit which must not be altered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referee reporting obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: After each match, the referee shall complete and sign the official FIFA report form ... note in as much detail as possible all occurrences, such as misconduct of players leading to caution or expulsion, unsporting behaviour by supporters and/or by officials ... and hand it over to the FIFA Match Commissioner at the stadium immediately after the match.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees must produce detailed match reports and retain a copy; reports are immediate post-match deliverables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary compliance and player conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary incidents are dealt with in compliance with the FIFA Disciplinary Code ... players agree in particular to: a) respect the spirit of fair play, non-violence and the authority of the match officials; b) behave accordingly; c) refrain from doping ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations fall to FIFA Disciplinary Committee; associations and members must follow anti-discrimination and anti‑match‑fixing obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical staffing and COVID-19 hygiene roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Each participating member association shall include a medical doctor in its delegation for each match. In addition, the host association shall appoint a medical response coordinator ... each participating member association shall appoint a lead hygiene implementation officer and a team medical liaison officer in accordance with the requirements of the IMP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific medical and hygiene roles are mandatory per IMP to manage health and COVID-19 protocols at matches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-competition medical assessment and player health protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Each participating member association shall ensure that its players undergo a pre-competition medical assessment prior to the start of the preliminary competition ... to detect heart issues or risk factors that may lead to sudden cardiac arrest ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associations must perform cardiovascular screening and other medical assessments before competition commencement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doping testing and prohibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Doping is strictly prohibited. The FIFA Anti-Doping Regulations, the FIFA Disciplinary Code and all other relevant FIFA regulations, circulars and directives shall apply ... Every player may be subject to in-competition testing ... and to out-of-competition testing at any time and place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full compliance with FIFA anti-doping regime required; random testing may occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concussion protocol and return-to-play
rubrics_metrics.description: A player who experiences a suspected concussion during a match must undergo an examination by the team doctor ... The referee may temporarily suspend play for up to three minutes whenever an incident of suspected concussion occurs. The team doctor will have the final decision ... FIFA recommends that teams follow the return to play protocol set forth in SCAT5 ... FIFA requires that before any player who suffers a concussion can return to play, the team doctor must certify that (a) such player has passed each of the steps set out in SCAT5, and that (b) such player is fit for competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Team doctor has authority to prevent return-to-play; SCAT5 is the recommended protocol; clinical judgment is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stadium entry COVID-19 test requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Proof of a negative test conducted no earlier than 72 hours before accessing the match stadium and in accordance with the provisions of the IMP must be provided in order for a Team Delegation Member to enter the match stadium and remain on the premises during matchday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negative test within 72 hours is mandatory for stadium access for every Team Delegation Member.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disputes and jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: All disputes ... shall be promptly settled by negotiation. Participating member associations, players and officials may not take disputes to an ordinary court of law but to the exclusive jurisdiction of FIFA ... sole recourse shall be to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) in Lausanne, Switzerland ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FIFA internal dispute resolution is mandatory; CAS is ultimate arbitral forum after FIFA channels are exhausted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protests: definition and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Protests are objections ... related to events or matters that have a direct effect on matches ... Protests shall be submitted in writing to the FIFA Match Commissioner within two hours of the match in question and followed up with a full written report ... within 24 hours of the end of the match, otherwise they shall be disregarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility protests and other pitch/equipment protests have specific timing rules (e.g., pitch state protests must be made before kick‑off to the referee).

rubrics_metrics.name: No protest against referee decisions on facts
rubrics_metrics.description: No protests may be made about the referee’s decisions regarding facts connected with play. Such decisions are final and not subject to appeal ... The same applies for any potential issue concerning the use of goal-line technology (GLT) and the video assistant referee (VAR) system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referee factual decisions, GLT and VAR determinations are not subject to protest or appeal under these Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for unfounded protests
rubrics_metrics.description: If an unfounded or irresponsible protest is lodged, the FIFA Disciplinary Committee may impose a fine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protests must meet formal conditions and be well-founded or risk financial sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start list / matchday squad composition and identification
rubrics_metrics.description: The start list must contain a minimum of 14 and a maximum of 23 players, one of which must be a goalkeeper. If there are fewer than 14 players available, FIFA will consider the matter and may make exceptions on a case-by-case basis. The 11 first-named players must start the match, and the remaining players on the start list are designated as substitutes. The numbers on the players’ shirts must correspond with the numbers indicated on the start list. All goalkeepers and the captain must be identified as such. At least one player must be a goalkeeper, up to a maximum of three, with the number 1 shirt reserved for one of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start lists must be returned to the referee at least 85 minutes before kick-off and conform to numbering and identity rules; permanent international passport is required as proof of identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Player identity documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The only document considered to be valid proof of a player’s identity and nationality shall be a permanent international passport that explicitly, and in Latin characters, states the player’s first name(s) and surname(s), as well as his day, month and year of birth. Identity cards or other local supporting official documents shall not be accepted ... A player without a valid permanent international passport shall not be entitled to play.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associations must present players' passports to the FIFA Match Commissioner on the day before the match.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement of players before kick-off and during match
rubrics_metrics.description: If any of the first 11 players named on the start list are not able to start the match for any reason, they may be replaced by any of the available substitutes. The replaced player(s) may no longer take part in the match, and the quota of substitute players shall be reduced accordingly. During the match, up to five players may still be replaced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitute quotas and in‑match replacement rules updated to reflect five substitution allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media accreditation, facilities and obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each association shall appoint a dedicated media officer ... coordinate media accreditation requests ... Both associations shall make their training sessions open to the media for at least 15 minutes on the day before the match ... An adequate number of covered seats shall be made available for the written press ... working area with desks, power supply and cabled or Wi-Fi internet connections shall also be provided ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host and visiting associations must provide media infrastructure, accreditation control, and provide access to training and pre/post-match media activities per FIFA guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview and mixed-zone rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews shall not be permitted during the match ... Post-match interviews ('flash' interviews) shall be conducted after the match in a designated area ... Associations shall make their head coach and at least two key players available for interviews. All players from both teams who are listed on the official start list are obliged to pass through the mixed zone ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media interactions are regulated: certain pre/post match availability is mandatory; dressing rooms and field access restricted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on media access to dressing rooms and pitch
rubrics_metrics.description: Media representatives are forbidden from entering the team and referee dressing rooms before, during and after the match. However, one of the host broadcaster’s cameras may enter the dressing rooms before the match ... No media representatives shall be allowed to enter the field of play before, during or after the match, with the exception of one hand-held camera crew covering the team line-ups at the start of the match and up to two of the host broadcaster’s cameras filming after the end of the match.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict limits on media physical access; exceptions tightly defined and require accreditation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial provisions and revenue ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: All revenue from the exploitation of the commercial rights ... for the preliminary competition matches belongs to the host association and, with the income from ticket sales, form the gross receipts. The owners of the rights are obliged to provide FIFA, upon request and free of charge, with 15 minutes of action footage per match. FIFA shall use this footage free of charge ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host keeps commercial proceeds but must supply footage to FIFA; levies to confederations deducted from gross receipts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost allocation and COVID-19 cost responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The participating member associations shall settle all other costs among themselves. FIFA recommends: a) visiting association pays international travel and delegation costs; b) host pays domestic transport for visiting delegation; c) host pays board and lodging for match officials ... e) all costs related to COVID-19 testing and documentation requested shall be borne by the association or team in question. f) all costs related to the COVID-19 preventative measures required at the match stadium shall be borne by the host association.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COVID-19 testing and prevention costs allocation is explicit: team/association pays testing/documentation; host pays stadium preventive measures; FIFA covers testing for FIFA delegation and match officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: FIFA costs borne by FIFA
rubrics_metrics.description: FIFA shall bear the cost of: a) international travel and daily allowances for the FIFA delegation members, match officials included, as determined by FIFA. b) COVID-19 testing of the FIFA delegation members, including match officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FIFA covers its own delegation travel and testing costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ticketing responsibilities and allocations
rubrics_metrics.description: The host association is responsible for ticketing ... shall set aside an appropriate number ... of complimentary and purchasable tickets for the visiting association. At least five representatives from the visiting association shall be seated in the VIP box. The host association shall, upon request and free of charge, provide FIFA with ten VIP box tickets and up to 40 category 1 tickets for each match.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ticket allocation must follow these minima; host may be required to include FIFA-prescribed terms and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability of host association
rubrics_metrics.description: The host association of a preliminary competition match shall be exclusively responsible for the organisation of its home matches and shall discharge FIFA from all responsibility and relinquish any claim against FIFA and the members of its delegation for any damages resulting from any claims relating to such match.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host assumes all liability and waives claims against FIFA for match-related damages (except neutral venue matches staged by FIFA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevailing regulations, language and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Matters not provided for ... shall be decided by FIFA. In the case of any discrepancy between these Regulations and any competition regulations issued by a confederation, the text of these Regulations shall prevail. In the case of any discrepancy in the interpretation of the English, French, Spanish or German texts of these Regulations, the English text shall be authoritative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FIFA has final interpretive and enforcement authority; English version controls for multilingual discrepancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright, waiver and no-waiver policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The copyright of the match schedule ... shall be the property of FIFA. Any waiver by FIFA of any breach of these Regulations shall not operate as, or be construed to be, a waiver of any other breach ... Any such waiver shall only be valid if given in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FIFA retains copyright and strict control over waivers; oral or implicit waivers are not valid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational guidelines and confederation implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to FIFA’s approval, the confederations are authorised to issue implementation rules and operational guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confederations may issue supplementary operational rules but they require FIFA approval and must not conflict with these Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stadium and matchday operational details (clocks, substitutions boards, smoking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clocks in the stadium showing the length of time played may run during the match ... The referee shall indicate the number of minutes to be allowed for time lost ... Panels or electronic display boards ... shall be used to indicate the substitution of players and the number of minutes to be allowed for time lost. Smoking is not permitted in the technical area or in the vicinity of the field of play ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational matchday elements must comply with FIFA instructions; display boards required for substitutions and added time; smoking prohibited in technical and competition areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footballs conformity
rubrics_metrics.description: The footballs used in the preliminary competition shall be supplied by the host association ... shall conform with the provisions of the Laws of the Game and the FIFA Equipment Regulations. They shall bear one of the following three designations: the official 'FIFA QUALITY PRO' logo, the official 'FIFA QUALITY' logo or the 'INTERNATIONAL MATCHBALL STANDARD (IMS)' logo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host provides match balls and visiting team should be provided sufficient balls for practice; balls must meet FIFA/Laws standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team equipment and no political/religious messages
rubrics_metrics.description: The participating member associations shall comply with the FIFA Equipment Regulations in force. The display of political, religious or personal messages or slogans in any language or form by players and officials on their playing or team kits, equipment ... or body is prohibited. The similar display of commercial messages and slogans ... is not allowed for the duration of their time at any official activity organised by FIFA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kits and equipment must comply with equipment regs; no political/religious/personal/commercial slogan display during official activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Player shirt numbering and badges
rubrics_metrics.description: Each player shall wear a number between 1 and 23 on the front and back of his team shirt and on his playing shorts. The colour of the numbers must contrast clearly ... It is not compulsory for the name of the player to appear on his shirt during the preliminary competition. FIFA shall supply a sufficient number of players’ sleeve badges with the official competition logo ... which shall be affixed on the right-hand sleeve ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbering and sleeve badge placement mandated; goalkeeper numbering and shirt provisions specified (number 1 reserved).
